title: Cross-layer anomaly atlas and adaptive trace-hook prioritization
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Goal: build an 'anomaly atlas' that correlates traces, synthetic probes, logs, metrics, and model-level error signals into a single dashboard and introduce an adaptive trace-hook prioritization policy so we capture high-value traces during error spikes without blowing ingest budgets. Scope: 1) data model and enrichment: extend trace hooks to attach standardized failure attributes (failure_type, model_response_code, token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit) and normalized upstream/downstream service tags; 2) ingestion pipeline: add ingestion transformations that compute a composite error score and causal-chain candidates; 3) adaptive sampling: implement a prioritization policy that increases sampling for services upstream of a composite score spike and for traces that include model_rejection or HTTP 5xx/gRPC UNAVAILABLE; 4) dashboard: new atlas view with heatmap by service x failure_type, causal chain explorer, and quick links to example traces and correlated logs. Why: current dashboards surface lane-level error rates but do not present likely causal chains or efficiently collect traces when incidents start. Trade-offs: adaptive sampling improves signal but risks missing rare pre‑error patterns in low-volume services; we will mitigate by deterministic capture of a small per-minute reservoir and targeted synthetic probes. This ticket includes design of the schema, a small ingestion transform, a trace-hook change with rollout plan, dashboard panels, and a lightweight cost model for sampling adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Trace hooks attach the standardized failure attributes on 95% of request paths (failure_type, model_response_code, token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit)
Ingestion transformation computes a composite error score and writes it to the observability index for dashboard consumption
Adaptive sampling policy implemented in trace-orchestrator that increases sample rate by factor configurable per service and decays automatically after 10 minutes
Atlas dashboard shows service x failure_type heatmap; selecting a cell surfaces top causal-chain candidates and links to 5 representative traces
End-to-end test using synthetic trace probes demonstrates sampling uprate during a simulated downstream model timeout and subsequent decay
Cost impact analysis included in the PR describing expected additional trace volume and estimated monthly cost delta
